Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={4}^{x}$ and $v(x)=tan⁡(x).$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={({4}^{x})}^{′}tan⁡(x)+{4}^{x}{(tan⁡(x))}^{′} \\  & =({4}^{x}ln⁡(4))tan⁡(x)+{4}^{x}({sec}^{2}⁡(x)) \\  & ={4}^{x}ln⁡(4)tan⁡(x)+{4}^{x}{sec}^{2}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$
